text:
maria: Hey team — prepping a 2-week POC for FinCorp. They want a Dedicated endpoint but their security team will only allowlist specific egress IPs.

maria: Questions: can we provide a small set of static egress IPs for the dedicated pool? What's the fastest path (hosted API key vs small dedicated pool) and any obvious blockers for a security review?

ajay: Short answer: yes, we can. Two common patterns: hosted API keys + customer open inbound to our public endpoints (no allowlist needed on our side), or spin a Dedicated pool with customer allowlisting our NATed egress IPs.

ajay: Tradeoffs: hosted = fastest (minutes) but customer has to trust public endpoints and can't pin capacity. Dedicated = provides fixed egress IPs and capacity guarantees, but provisioning + IP allocation takes a bit longer.

leo: Netops detail: we can allocate a set of static public IPs (typically 2-5) for a Dedicated pool. Need to know whether the customer requires a single IP per pool or a CIDR range. Also: do they want IP rotation during the POC?

leo: FYI: some orgs require ptr/rDNS or hostnames for monitoring — we can provide reverse DNS for allocated IPs if requested.

maria: FinCorp asked for only 3 IPs to keep firewall rules small. They also want a short TTL for any rotation schedule (they prefer no rotation during POC).

tess: On infra: Dedicated endpoints egress through our NAT gateway assigned to that pool. We'll record the mapping pool_id -> [public IPs] and share. Example response customers can allowlist:

```
POOL: dedicated-fincorp-01
EGRESS_IPS: 54.33.12.101, 54.33.12.102, 54.33.12.103
HOSTNAME: api.dedicated.redwood.ai
```

tess: For quick testing you can also provide them a temporary API key scoped to the dedicated pool; that key will only work against that pool hostname.

leo: Network note: outbound DNS and OCSP/CRL checks will open ephemeral outbound connections to the public internet. If the customer's firewall only allows our three IPs, they must also allow DNS resolver IPs or point at an internal resolver. Document this for them.

maria: Good call. Also they asked: "Can you restrict outbound traffic from the Dedicated pool to specific domains only?" Security asked for domain allowlisting.

ajay: We can implement domain-level egress restrictions via an outbound proxy/firewall on the pool, but it's more invasive and can break function-calling or webhook flows. Workable for a POC if they accept limited functionality.

infra-bot: Created NET-TICKET-5234: allocate 3 static egress IPs for pool dedicated-fincorp-01. Assigned to leo. ETA 48h.

leo: Next steps for ops: need customer point of contact, their firewall CIDR format (do they accept single IPs or /32 entries), and whether they want reverse DNS. I'll attach the ticket when done.

maria: Customer contact is jane.d@fincorp.com. They accept single IP entries (/32). Reverse DNS not required for POC.

tess: Pricing note (internal): Dedicated pools include the NAT egress IP allocation, but if FinCorp pushes large egress traffic to customer infra (downloads/uploads) we should flag network egress transfer charges. Sales: mark this on the quote as "potential cloud egress".

maria: Noted — I'll add a line item. Can we give them a one-paragraph connection instructions to drop into their firewall ticket?

ajay: Draft snippet for customer firewall:

```
Allow outbound TCP 443 to:
  54.33.12.101/32
  54.33.12.102/32
  54.33.12.103/32
Ensure DNS to a resolver that can resolve public hostnames (or allow DNS egress to your resolver IPs).
Allow OCSP/CRL (TCP 80/443) for certificate validation where applicable.
```

maria: Perfect. Can we confirm expected timeline and rollback plan if something fails? They want to start next Tue.

leo: Timeline: reserve IPs and provision pool in ~48 hours after ticket. Share IPs and test endpoints. If anything breaks we can fall back to hosted API keys for testing (no IP allowlist from their side) within 1 hour.

tess: Private/VPC option: if FinCorp wants full network isolation we can do a VPC peering / PrivateLink setup but that's ~2-3 weeks and requires their network team to run BGP/peering or accept route tables. Not suitable for a 2-week POC.

maria: Great — ok let's provision the 3 IPs and create the dedicated-fincorp-01 pool. Please keep me in the loop on NET-TICKET-5234. Thanks :thumbsup:

infra-bot: NET-TICKET-5234 updated: provisioning started. ETA 36h. Assigned engineers: leo, tess.

maria: Thanks all. I'll pass the firewall snippet to Jane and request confirmation they can add /32s ASAP.
